title: Better Convergence Guarantees for Sign-Based Momentum Methods: the MVSM-v2 last-iterate convergence guarantee (printed as Theorem 4.4)
author: Wei Jiang, Dingzhi Yu, Sifan Yang, Wenhao Yang, Zechao Li, Lijun Zhang
work: Better Convergence Guarantees for Sign-Based Momentum Methods
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Theorem 4.4 (source0.tex lines 1003--1008, source label thm4), "Under Assumptions 1, 6, 7 and 8, set beta in (0,1] and eta = O(1/sqrt(dT)). Then MVSM-v2 satisfies E||grad f(x_tau)||_2 = O(d^{1/4} T^{-1/4})", delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 1324--1430 (107 lines, the article's appendix section "Proof of Theorem 4.4", a detached section-level proof block: the article uses no proof environment for it). The proof is the article's main distributed convergence argument and is not routine. It first controls the two-stage compression: the composed sign W = S_1((1/n) sum_j S_G(v_t^j)) is shown unbiased for vbar_t/G and its error e_t = v_t - vbar_t/G is shown to have zero mean and second moment at most d, using only the bounded-gradient assumption and the unbiasedness of the article's S_R operation. It then introduces a virtual iterate y_t = x_t - c_beta vbar_{t-1} with c_beta = eta(1-beta)/(G beta), proves the exact recursion y_{t+1} = y_t - (eta/G) gbar_t - eta e_t that turns the compressed method into an unbiased stochastic step plus bounded noise, and bounds the virtual displacement ||y_t - x_t|| <= eta sqrt(d) (1-beta)/beta. Because the initialization v_1 = g_1 forces y_2 - x_1 = -eta v_1 - c_beta gbar_1, the first step is treated separately, giving the sharper coefficient eta/(G beta); the later steps use smoothness, the inequality -<u,w> <= -||w||^2/2 + ||u-w||^2/2 and the second-moment bound to reach a one-step descent inequality. Summing the two descent inequalities over T steps, using f(y_{T+1}) >= f_* and choosing eta = gamma/sqrt(dT), yields a bound on the averaged squared gradient norm, and Jensen's inequality with the uniform output index tau converts it into the stated rate O(d^{1/4} T^{-1/4}). The substantive content is the virtual-iterate construction, the exact first-step separation and the two-stage compression moment computation; none of these is an unpacking of definitions. H3: a complete original research-paper proof of a main convergence theorem, 107 lines of genuinely technical stochastic-optimization analysis whose hypotheses are all retained, rather than a short verification of a known fact.
